message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.6","text":"Nevertheless, although the origin was one, many divisions of kingship arose in this way. The Persians were the first to take coals from the lightning that had fallen from heaven and preserve them with fuel of their own. They gave the fire special honor as a heavenly god, and because they were the first to worship it, they were the first to be honored with kingship by that very fire. After them, the Babylonians stole coals from the fire there, brought them safely into their own lands, and worshiped it; they too reigned next in succession. The Egyptians acted likewise and in their own language called the fire Phthae, which is interpreted “Hephaestus”; the one who first reigned among them is also called by his name. Thus those who reigned in each locality followed this practice, made an image, and kindled altars in honor of the fire. Most of them were extinguished from kingship;","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς ὑπαρχῆς μιᾶς οὔσης","chosen":"although the origin was one","rationale":"ὑπαρχή can denote an origin, beginning, underlying basis, or established state. “Origin” fits the following account of how multiple divisions of kingship arose, though “although the underlying basis was one” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τῇ οἰκείᾳ διεφύλαξαν τροφῇ","chosen":"preserve them with fuel of their own","rationale":"τροφή ordinarily denotes nourishment or sustenance; in relation to coals, “fuel” conveys what feeds and preserves the fire."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὰ ἑαυτῶν","chosen":"into their own lands","rationale":"The substantivized neuter plural is elliptical and could refer to their own places, territory, or possessions. “Lands” contextually expresses the transfer from the Persian fire to Babylonia."},{"source_quote":"Φθάε καλέσαντες, ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Ἥφαιστος","chosen":"called the fire Phthae, which is interpreted “Hephaestus”","rationale":"The Egyptian designation is transliterated, while the author’s Greek identification introduced by ἑρμηνεύεται is translated rather than harmonized with another naming tradition."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ἵδρυμα ποιήσαντες","chosen":"made an image","rationale":"ἵδρυμα can denote an erected sacred image, a shrine, or a sacred establishment. “Image” is chosen in view of the ξόανα mentioned immediately afterward, while “made a shrine” remains a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῆς μὲν βασιλείας οἱ πλεῖστοι ἀπεσβέσθησαν","chosen":"Most of them were extinguished from kingship","rationale":"The marked extinguishing metaphor is retained because it echoes the preceding fire imagery. The sense is that most lost their kingship, but that smoother wording would erase the wordplay."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.7","text":"Yet they did not cease reverencing the carved images, because of the wicked contrivance of the Magi, who devised for them pretexts capable of holding them fast to futile worship. For, after installing the images with magical rites, they appointed festivals for them consisting of sacrifices, libations, flutes, and clapping. Deceived under cover of these things, the senseless—even though their kingship had been taken away—do not abandon the accumulated religious observances. To such an extent, because of their love of pleasure, did they prefer error to truth. These people also, after becoming drunk, raise a ritual cry beside the altar, while their soul, from its depths as if through dreams, foretells to them the punishment that is to come for such deeds of theirs.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν κακὴν τῶν μάγων ἐπίνοιαν","chosen":"the wicked contrivance of the Magi","rationale":"μάγοι can denote Magi or magicians. “Magi” preserves the historically specific designation, while the magical rites in the context make the polemical sense clear."},{"source_quote":"εὑρόντων αὐτοῖς προφάσεις κρατεῖν αὐτοὺς πρὸς τὴν ματαίαν λατρείαν δυναμένας","chosen":"who devised for them pretexts capable of holding them fast to futile worship","rationale":"εὑρίσκω here concerns finding or devising pretexts, and κρατεῖν conveys keeping the worshipers under control or holding them fast."},{"source_quote":"ἱδρύσαντες γὰρ αὐτὰ μαγικαῖς τελεταῖς ἑορτὰς αὐτοῖς ὥρισαν","chosen":"For, after installing the images with magical rites, they appointed festivals for them","rationale":"The explanatory γάρ is represented by “For.” The participle is read temporally, while ἱδρύω can denote setting up, installing, or ritually establishing an image."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ τε θυμάτων, σπονδῶν, αὐλῶν τε καὶ κρότων","chosen":"consisting of sacrifices, libations, flutes, and clapping","rationale":"κρότοι can denote clapping, striking sounds, noisy applause, or clashing. “Clapping” supplies a concrete festival sound, though “clashing sounds” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"τῶν συνελθουσῶν θρησκειῶν","chosen":"the accumulated religious observances","rationale":"Literally, these are religious observances that have “come together.” “Accumulated” treats them as observances combined in the festivals; “combined religious observances” or “assembled rites” are alternatives."},{"source_quote":"παραβώμιον ἐπολολύζουσιν","chosen":"raise a ritual cry beside the altar","rationale":"ὀλολύζω denotes a loud ritual cry or ululation, while παραβώμιον locates the action beside the altar."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.8","text":"Therefore, with many forms of worship having passed through the world, we—the good merchants—are here bringing you the form of worship handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, like a pearl, displaying it and placing it before your judgment and at your disposal. Choose what seems good to you. If, then, you choose what is ours, you will not only be able to escape demons and the sufferings caused by demons, but, as you yourselves put them to flight and are implored by them, you will also enjoy the good things that will exist forever.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πολλῶν οὖν ἐν βίῳ παρελθουσῶν θρησκειῶν","chosen":"Therefore, with many forms of worship having passed through the world","rationale":"“Therefore” explicitly represents the inferential οὖν. The genitive absolute is rendered circumstantially; it could also be understood concessively, “Therefore, although many forms of worship have passed through the world.” The phrase ἐν βίῳ may mean “in life” or, contextually, “in the world.”"},{"source_quote":"πάρεσμεν φέροντες ὑμῖν (οἱ ἀγαθοὶ ἔμποροι) ἐκ προγόνων ἡμῖν παραδοθείσης καὶ φυλαχθείσης θρησκείας ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην","chosen":"we—the good merchants—are here bringing you the form of worship handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, like a pearl","rationale":"The presentation by the speakers is retained before the description of the inherited worship, following the supplied clause order. The genitive θρησκείας is represented idiomatically as what is brought and compared to a pearl; a more formally genitival interpretation is “bringing you, like a pearl, something from or of the worship handed down to us.”"},{"source_quote":"οἱ ἀγαθοὶ ἔμποροι","chosen":"we—the good merchants","rationale":"The nominative phrase is appositional to the implied subject of πάρεσμεν and continues the pearl-merchant image."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ κρίσει καὶ ἐξουσίᾳ τιθέντες","chosen":"placing it before your judgment and at your disposal","rationale":"κρίσις denotes judgment or evaluation, while ἐξουσία can denote authority, freedom of action, or power of disposal. The rendering preserves both the evaluation and the hearers’ freedom to choose."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ὑμῖν δοκοῦν ἐπιλέξασθε","chosen":"Choose what seems good to you","rationale":"The substantivized participle denotes what appears good or suitable to the hearers without asserting that their choice is objectively correct."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἡμέτερα ἕλησθε","chosen":"you choose what is ours","rationale":"The neuter plural leaves the referent broad enough to include the speakers’ teaching, worship, and practices."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοὶ αὐτὰ φυγαδεύοντες καὶ ἱκετευόμενοι ὑπ’ αὐτῶν","chosen":"as you yourselves put them to flight and are implored by them","rationale":"The neuter αὐτά can collect both the demons and the demonic sufferings just mentioned, whereas the masculine αὐτῶν most naturally refers specifically to the demons. The English pronouns preserve that referential breadth."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.9","text":"For otherwise, while in the present life you are abused by demons with strange afflictions, upon release from the body you will also have your souls punished forever—in truth, not because God condemns them, but because evil deeds carry such a judgment. For the demons, having authority through the food rendered to them, are admitted by your own hands into your own bodies. For, after dwelling in the innermost recesses for a long time, they also become blended with the soul. And because of the negligence of those who do not think to help themselves, or are even unwilling to do so, the soul of these very people, united to the demon when the body is dissolved, must be carried by it to whatever places it wishes. Worst of all, when, at the consummation of all things, the demon is first handed over to the purifying fire, the soul blended with it must itself be punished inexpressibly, while the demon takes pleasure. For the soul, since it comes from light, cannot bear the flame of the fire, which is foreign to its kind, and is tormented; but the demon, being within the substance of its own kind, takes immense pleasure, having become a bond hard to break for the soul that, under its influence, shares its condition.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ δαιμόνων ἀλλοκότοις πάθεσιν ἐνυβριζόμενοι","chosen":"you are abused by demons with strange afflictions","rationale":"ἐνυβρίζω conveys abusive or outrageous treatment, while ἀλλόκοτος denotes what is strange, alien, or extraordinary."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος ἀπαλλαγῇ καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς εἰσαεὶ κολασθησομένας ἕξετε","chosen":"upon release from the body you will also have your souls punished forever","rationale":"The future passive participle κολασθησομένας states that punishment will actually be inflicted on the souls, not merely that they will face its possibility. The construction with ἕξετε is retained rather than recast as a wholly impersonal prediction."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἀληθῆ οὐ θεοῦ καταδικάζοντος, ἀλλὰ κακῶν πράξεων τοιαύτην ἐχουσῶν κρίσιν","chosen":"in truth, not because God condemns them, but because evil deeds carry such a judgment","rationale":"τὰ ἀληθῆ functions adverbially as “in truth.” The contrasting genitive constructions deny that God’s condemnation is the cause and attribute the judgment to the character of evil deeds; the object “them” is supplied from the souls just mentioned."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τῆς αὐτοῖς ἀποδοθείσης τροφῆς","chosen":"through the food rendered to them","rationale":"ἀποδίδω can mean give back, render, or deliver what is due. “Rendered” preserves the implication of food presented to demons rather than ordinary eating alone."},{"source_quote":"ἐνδομυχήσαντες γὰρ πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ καὶ τῇ ψυχῇ ἀνακίρνανται","chosen":"For, after dwelling in the innermost recesses for a long time, they also become blended with the soul","rationale":"“For” represents the explanatory γάρ, and “also” represents καί. ἐνδομυχέω depicts dwelling or making a lair deep within, while ἀνακίρναμαι denotes becoming mixed or blended."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἑαυτοῖς βοηθεῖν μὴ νοούντων ἢ καὶ μὴ βουλομένων","chosen":"those who do not think to help themselves, or are even unwilling to do so","rationale":"νοέω with an infinitive can concern thinking of, considering, or intending an action. “Do not think to help themselves” avoids narrowing the phrase to ignorance about how to help; “do not intend to help themselves” is also viable."},{"source_quote":"ἀπορρήτως κολάζεσθαι","chosen":"be punished inexpressibly","rationale":"ἀπορρήτως can mean unspeakably, indescribably, or in a manner that cannot be disclosed. “Inexpressibly” preserves this uncertainty without reducing the punishment to something merely secret."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἀλλόφυλον τοῦ πυρὸς φλόγα","chosen":"the flame of the fire, which is foreign to its kind","rationale":"ἀλλόφυλος literally describes something belonging to another race or kind. The flame is represented as foreign to the soul that comes from light, in contrast to the demon’s affinity with the fire."},{"source_quote":"δεσμὸς δύσρηκτος","chosen":"a bond hard to break","rationale":"δύσρηκτος describes something difficult to break or rupture without necessarily asserting absolute impossibility."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ συμπαθείσης ψυχῆς","chosen":"for the soul that, under its influence, shares its condition","rationale":"συμπαθέω can mean sharing a condition, being affected together, suffering together, or having affinity, while ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ may express agency or causal influence. The rendering takes the soul as sharing the demon’s joined condition under its influence, not necessarily its pleasurable response to the fire. Alternatives include “for the soul that suffers together with it because of it” and “for the soul affected along with it under its power.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἱ γὰρ δαίμονες, διὰ τῆς αὐτοῖς ἀποδοθείσης τροφῆς ἐξουσίαν ἔχοντες, ὑπὸ τῶν ὑμετέρων χειρῶν εἰς τὰ ὑμέτερα εἰσκρίνεται σώματα","issue":"The selected edition prints the singular verb εἰσκρίνεται with the plural subject οἱ δαίμονες and plural participle ἔχοντες. The English represents the contextually clear plural sense, but a plural Greek form would be a conjectural grammatical normalization rather than the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"εἰσκρίνονται","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.10","text":"As for the demons’ eagerness to slip into human bodies, this is the cause. Being spirits and having desire for foods, drinks, and intercourse, yet being unable to partake because they are spirits and need instruments suited to their use, they enter human bodies so that, obtaining them as instruments that serve them, they may be able to obtain what they want—whether foods through a person’s teeth or intercourse through that person’s genitals. Consequently, to put demons to flight, deprivation, fasting, and hardship are the most fitting aid. For if they enter a human body for the sake of partaking, it is clear that hardship drives them out. But since some are more formidable and, after persisting obstinately, remain in the body undergoing punishment even though they themselves are being punished, it is therefore necessary to take refuge in God with prayers and supplications, while abstaining from every occasion of impurity, so that God’s hand may be able to touch that person for healing, as someone who is pure and believes.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοὺς δαίμονας γλίχεσθαι εἰς τὰ ἀνθρώπων εἰσδύειν σώματα","chosen":"the demons’ eagerness to slip into human bodies","rationale":"γλίχομαι expresses eager desire or striving, while εἰσδύω depicts entering or slipping into something."},{"source_quote":"εἰς βρωτὰ καὶ ποτὰ καὶ συνουσίαν","chosen":"for foods, drinks, and intercourse","rationale":"Although συνουσία can denote association more generally, the subsequent reference to the genitals establishes sexual intercourse in this context."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ὑπουργούντων ὀργάνων τυχόντες","chosen":"obtaining them as instruments that serve them","rationale":"ὑπουργέω describes rendering subordinate service. Human bodies are treated as instrumental agents through which the demons satisfy their desires."},{"source_quote":"ἡ ἔνδεια καὶ ἡ νηστεία καὶ ἡ κακουχία","chosen":"deprivation, fasting, and hardship","rationale":"ἔνδεια denotes lack or deprivation, while κακουχία denotes harsh bodily treatment, hardship, or privation. The distinct terms are retained rather than collapsed into fasting alone."},{"source_quote":"ἔνια δεινότερα τυγχάνοντα προσφιλονεικήσαντα καίτοι τιμωρούμενα τῷ τιμωρουμένῳ προσμένει σώματι","chosen":"some are more formidable and, after persisting obstinately, remain in the body undergoing punishment even though they themselves are being punished","rationale":"The neuter plural refers to some demons. καίτοι τιμωρούμενα states that the demons are being punished, while τῷ τιμωρουμένῳ σώματι separately describes the body as undergoing punishment; the singular verb with a neuter plural subject is regular Greek agreement."},{"source_quote":"προσφιλονεικήσαντα","chosen":"after persisting obstinately","rationale":"The compound conveys continued contentious resistance or stubborn persistence, fitting demons that remain despite punishment."},{"source_quote":"ἀπεχομένους τε πάσης ἀκαθάρτου προφάσεως","chosen":"while abstaining from every occasion of impurity","rationale":"πρόφασις can mean pretext, occasion, ostensible cause, or excuse. “Occasion” best fits practical abstention, though “every impure pretext” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ χεὶρ εἰς ἴασιν αὐτοῦ ἐπιψαῦσαι δυνηθῇ ὡς ἁγνοῦ καὶ πιστεύοντος","chosen":"God’s hand may be able to touch that person for healing, as someone who is pure and believes","rationale":"ἐπιψαύω governs the genitive αὐτοῦ. Although the pronoun follows a reference to the body, the masculine participles ἁγνοῦ and πιστεύοντος identify the referent as the afflicted person."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
